conditions: Exact mechanics: SAS takes the more favorable of the SAS and ATL picks; ATL takes the more favorable of the remaining ATL/SAS pick and CLE's pick; CLE gets whatever is left (always the least favorable of the three). Exception to the ranks: if CLE's native pick is the most favorable of the three, ATL gets rank 1 and SAS rank 2.

CLE's pick enters only after UTA's swap rights: if UTA's slot is 1-8, UTA takes the most favorable of the UTA, MIN and CLE picks, so the item facing ATL is the less favorable of CLE's pick and UTA's pick. This UTA linkage is not encoded; it only matters if CLE's pick beats UTA's top-8 pick.

ATL.text: Chained swaps: SAS takes the better of SAS/ATL; ATL then takes the better of the leftover and CLE's pick; CLE gets the remaining pick (worst of the three). CLE's pick is first exposed to UTA's swap right.

open_issues: Source availability: no post-deadline 'Checking In On Traded 2026 First-Round Picks' article (published in earlier years) was found; the Hoops Rumors 'What Teams Got In Return For Their Traded 2026 Draft Picks' (2026-03-21) is paywalled. Conditions come from the 'Traded First-Round Picks For 2026 NBA Draft' page (dated 2025-08-27 but already reflecting the Feb 2026 deadline deals), cross-checked against the deadline recap and individual trade reports.

UTA/MIN/CLE/DET/ATL/SAS six-team chain: the full rule (UTA swap rights over MIN and CLE if UTA is top 8; DET-MIN protected swap; CLE-ATL swap; ATL-SAS swap) cannot be written as one rank-based pool. It is encoded as UTA protected [1-8]->OKC plus two pools (DET/MIN and ATL/CLE/SAS), which is exact only when UTA's pick is in 1-8 AND more favorable than both MIN's and CLE's. That held with near-certainty after the deadline (UTA bottom-5; MIN, CLE playoff teams) and in the realized draft (UTA #2). Confidence set to low for these six natives for that reason. The exact rule (all branches) is implemented in router_2026.py (route/Router2026); use that module, not these pool objects, for simulation.

UTA 9-30 branch: the bottom section of the Hoops Rumors 2026 page states that if UTA's pick lands outside the top 8 it goes to OKC, DET gets the better of its own and MIN's pick (MIN keeps its own if in the top 19), and the UTA/MIN picks are not in play for ATL/CLE (ATL-CLE swap uses CLE's own pick); UTA then has no first. Encoded in router_2026.py.

Remaining interpretation choices in the six-team chain (flagged as ASSUMPTIONS in router_2026.py): UTA's best-of right is resolved as a swap with MIN then CLE (the order that reproduces Hoops Rumors' closed form for the pick facing ATL); DET's 1-19 protection applies only to MIN's own pick, so DET can swap for UTA's pick if MIN received it. Hoops Rumors' closed forms for DET/MIN are internally inconsistent when MIN's own pick is in 1-19 (both formulas would assign DET's pick), so a sequential reading is used. None of these branches occurred.

WAS/PHX: WAS's top-8-protected pick also carries a swap right with PHX (WAS takes the better) if WAS is 1-8; not encoded in WAS's rule. Exact only when WAS's pick beats PHX's, which held (WAS worst record, #1 pick; PHX pick #16). Confidence low for WAS, MEM, ORL, PHX; MEM/ORL/PHX pool rests on one source (Hoops Rumors) for its terms, though the realized outcome matches. The WAS 9-30 branch (pick to NYK, PHX's pick enters the MEM/CHA group, WAS has no first) is stated explicitly by Hoops Rumors and encoded in router_2026.py.

OKC/HOU/LAC pool, HOU 1-4 branch (not stated in sources): HOU keeps its pick; CBS Philadelphia's report on the McCain trade states that PHI gets the more favorable of OKC/LAC, which router_2026.py follows, and DAL getting the other is an assumption. Source conflict: Hoops Rumors' McCain-trade report (2026-02) calls PHI's asset 'Houston's 2026 first-round pick (which the Thunder control)', whereas the Hoops Rumors 2026 pick page and deadline recap describe it as the second-most favorable of OKC/HOU/LAC; under the former, PHI would get nothing in this branch. Realized outcome (HOU #22 to PHI) is consistent with both; the branch did not occur.

Pick 13 (MIA): Miami made the selection; the pick was part of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade reported on the eve of the draft (June 23, 2026) and completed July 6. Recorded holder = MIA (holder before the draft-period trade); Hoops Rumors' order/results pages list it as 'Bucks (from Heat)'. Not a deadline-state mismatch; native rule is own.

Draft-period trades (not mismatches): 16 MEM->OKC, 17 OKC->DET (via MEM), 21 DET->MEM, 24 NYK->LAL, 25 LAL->DAL (via NYK), 26 DEN->SAS, 28 MIN->BKN, 29 CLE->SAC, 30 DAL->PHX (via NYK). Realized holders are recorded before these trades.

Hoops Rumors' post-play-in projection (2026-04-18) had MEM at 16 via ORL and CHA at 17 via PHX with PHI's pick at 18; after tiebreak drawings the final order was PHX 16 (to MEM), PHI 17 (to OKC), ORL 18 (to CHA), confirmed by Wikipedia, Hoops Rumors results and NBA.com. Final order used.

Wikipedia labels pick 30 as 'Dallas (from Oklahoma City, Washington and Philadelphia)'; the post-deadline chain per Hoops Rumors is OKC pool rank 3 -> WAS (pre-deadline) -> DAL (Anthony Davis trade, Feb 2026). The PHI mention is not explained by the sources but does not change the deadline holder (DAL).
No 2026 first-round picks were forfeited (Wikipedia: first draft since 2021 with 60 picks).

POST_DEADLINE_CHANGES is empty: Hoops Rumors' 2026 offseason trade list shows no 2026 first moved between the deadline and the draft; the earliest such trade is the draft-day (June 23) MEM-OKC #16/#17 deal. The MIA #13 / Giannis deal was agreed the night before round 1 but completed July 6 with Miami selecting, so it is treated like the 2025 module's agreed-but-completed-later trades (holder = MIA).
